title: Dedicated request queue prioritization and adaptive surge strategy - Q2 roadmap
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: During multi-tenant demand spikes we see uneven request latencies and degraded tail-SLOs from indiscriminate queueing and blunt pool-level autoscaling. Objective: Define and deliver a prioritized request queuing and adaptive surge strategy that reduces high-percentile latency by 25% for impacted customers while limiting incremental GPU cost to <8% of baseline for typical workloads. Scope: prioritization rules, request classification (latency-sensitive vs batchable), burst lanes for committed customers, integration points with existing routing/policy engine, fallback model variants for graceful degradation. Out of scope: hardware procurement, fundamental kernel-level runtime changes (except instrumentation hooks).
acceptance_criteria: Prioritization policy is configurable in Console and via API with at least three priority tiers
End-to-end perf test demonstrates >=25% reduction in P99 latency for latency-sensitive workload during simulated surge
Autoscale policy can trigger a limited-cost surge lane with budget guardrails and rollback on sustained cost thresholds
Documentation (Console help + PRD) published and linked in roadmap
Canary rollout plan with success criteria defined and validated on Dedicated staging clusters
deliverables: Design doc: request class tagging and priority arbitration algorithm
API/Console UI spec for priority configuration
Autoscale surge lane implementation with budget cap and metrics
E2E perf harness and synthetic surge scenarios
Runbook for on-call and SRE for surge incidents
Customer-facing plan for opt-in and migration guidance
metrics: P99 latency for marked latency-sensitive routes (baseline vs post-change)
Average cost delta per cluster during surge windows
Successful request rate for high-priority lanes vs baseline
Percentage of surges recovered without manual intervention
Number of customers migrated to configured priority lanes
risks: Incorrect priority rules could starve batch workloads leading to regressions in throughput
Overly aggressive surge lanes may exceed committed budget or degrade multitenant fairness
Complexity in tying priority config to billing/quotas could create billing disputes
Console UX may add cognitive load; misconfigurations from PMs/SEs are possible
Integration with existing routing policies may expose race conditions under network partitions
stakeholders: Legal: compliance review on surge billing language
